title: You Are the Key: Never Ignore Your Self-Story
author: Dominic Salles
summary: This is Chapter 5 of Dominic Salles's Head of Department Manifesto, and it argues that the stories people tell about themselves quietly set the limits of what they attempt. Salles opens with a vivid account of his parents' risk-taking, boom-and-bust life and the self-story it gave him: that anyone can achieve anything if they think ahead. He cites stereotype-threat studies, in which reminding students of group stereotypes lowered performance, to show how powerful such narratives are. He then lists 32 limiting beliefs common among teachers across behaviour, marking, pedagogy, exams, SEND, leadership and workload, and calls them all wrong. His practical claim is that checklists beat persuasion, because success from following a checklist changes beliefs afterwards, so it is 'checklist first, hearts and minds second'. The chapter closes with the case for optimism, citing its health benefits, and applies it to a head of department facing two difficult Year 9 classes by shrinking the problem to four ringleaders.
points: Self-stories shaped by upbringing and environment either restrict or open up career possibilities, and stereotype-threat studies show how easily they can change performance.
Salles argues that you cannot win teachers over by arguing with their beliefs; give them a checklist, let success follow, and the beliefs will change afterwards.
His list of 32 limiting beliefs spans behaviour, marking, curriculum, exams, SEND, leadership and workload and is a handy diagnostic for a department team.
Optimism is trainable through visualising a realistic best self, separating what is in your control from what is not, and changing the language you use.
Reframing a 'challenging class' as four students who influence the other twenty-four turns a vague problem into a solvable one.
quotes: The stories we tell ourselves are incredibly powerful. We often accept narratives about ourselves which work against us.

I have found repeatedly that it is impossible to win enough hearts and minds by dealing with people’s beliefs. But as soon as success happens, because of the checklist, beliefs change. Checklist first, hearts and minds second.
We all have limiting beliefs imposed on us by our environment – by our experience of school. A checklist helps you override this – you follow it, even if your beliefs don’t match.

Understanding your self-story will help you understand both your potential – which is much greater than you think – and your limiting beliefs, which, for most of us – are even greater than we would like to admit.
Balance your aspirations with an accurate understanding of what is actually within your control, ensuring that your goals are grounded rather than mere wishful thinking.
This is not ‘a challenging class’. It is a class with 4 students who influence too many of the other 24. You just have to solve four kids - that’s all they are.
School is like that. It is full of absurd and difficult miniature trials. The jargon of the day is that they are full of “wicked problems”.
